Implemented `parse_amount` in `ledgerly/importers.py`:

- Strips surrounding whitespace and accepts an optional leading `$`.
- Accepts plain digits or properly grouped thousands separators (`1,234`, `1,234,567`).
- Allows at most two decimal places.
- Rejects negatives, malformed separators, empty text, and non-string input with `BillingError("invalid_amount", ...)`.
- Returns a `Decimal` and has an explicit return annotation.

All 10 tests pass, including the existing `parse_amount("$1,234.50") == 1234.5` check.

Implemented `parse_amount` in `ledgerly/importers.py`:

- Strips surrounding whitespace and accepts an optional leading `$`.
- Accepts plain digits or properly grouped thousands separators (`1,234`, `1,234,567`).
- Allows at most two decimal places.
- Rejects negatives, malformed separators, empty text, and non-string input with `BillingError("invalid_amount", ...)`.
- Returns a `Decimal` and has an explicit return annotation.

All 10 tests pass, including the existing `parse_amount("$1,234.50") == 1234.5` check.
